findings.title: request.referer injected into a JavaScript string with only HTML escaping
findings.body: The embed layout interpolates request.referer directly into a single-quoted JS string: parent.postMessage({...}, '<%= request.referer %>'). ERB output is HTML-escaped, which is the wrong escaping context for a JavaScript string — and in the Rails 3 boot mode this repo still supports, ERB's html_escape does not escape single quotes at all. A request to /embed/best with a Referer such as http://<embeddable-host>/';alert(1);// passes the ensure_embeddable host check (a single quote and semicolons are legal characters in a URI path) and breaks out of the JS string, executing arbitrary script inside the iframe on the forum's own origin. Use request.referer.to_json (or escape_javascript) when building the targetOrigin string.

findings.title: Unescaped URL interpolated into href attribute of posts rendered as raw HTML
findings.body: TopicEmbed.import appends an 'Imported from' footer built as "#{url}" with the URL inserted unescaped. The only validation is that the URL starts with http(s)://; a single quote is a valid URI character, so a feed item link or an embed URL like http://host/page'onmouseover='alert(1) breaks out of the href attribute and injects arbitrary attributes/markup into the post body. Because these posts are created with cook_method raw_html, Post#cook returns the raw string with no sanitization, and the embed view renders it via `raw post.cooked` (and the main site renders cooked verbatim), this becomes stored XSS on the forum origin for everyone who views the imported topic or embed. Escape the URL (e.g. ERB::Util.html_escape) before interpolating it into the attribute.

findings.title: raw_html cook method renders remotely fetched content with zero sanitization
findings.body: Post#cook now returns `raw` unchanged when cook_method is raw_html, bypassing PrettyText's sanitizer entirely. The content stored in these posts comes from remote sources: feed items via PollFeed (no filtering at all) and arbitrary pages on the embeddable host via TopicRetriever/import_remote (ruby-readability whitelists tags/attributes but still passes through href/src values such as javascript: URLs). Any script, event handler, or javascript: link in the source HTML is rendered verbatim on topic pages, in the embed iframe on the forum origin, in email digests, etc. Additionally, PostCreator now honors opts[:cook_method] for every caller (lib/post_creator.rb setup_post) — if request parameters ever flow into PostCreator opts, any user could create unsanitized raw-HTML posts, so this must be guarded against.

findings.title: Feed items without content crash the polling job permanently
findings.body: `CGI.unescapeHTML(i.content.scrub)` raises NoMethodError when an item has no content element. With simple-rss, RSS 2.0 items only expose #content when the feed includes <content:encoded>; a large number of feeds carry only <description>, and Atom entries may omit content too. One such item raises out of the each loop, aborting the whole poll (the job has retry: false), and since items are processed in feed order the same item crashes the job again on every hourly run, so no later items are ever imported. Fall back to i.description / to_s and wrap per-item processing so one bad item cannot kill the entire feed poll.

findings.title: TopicEmbed row is created even when PostCreator rolled the post back, leaving a dangling reference
findings.body: import only checks `if post.present?` before calling TopicEmbed.create!, but PostCreator#create returns the unsaved post object (with errors) when creation fails — for example when rollback_if_host_spam_detected fires, which happens for a trust-level-0 embed user importing an article that links several times to the same host (newuser_spam_host_threshold). In that case the inner Post transaction rolls back the topic and post inserts, but TopicEmbed.create! still commits a row whose topic_id/post_id point at records that no longer exist. Every subsequent /embed/best request for that URL then finds the dead topic_id and TopicView raises not-found/invalid-access, so the embed for that URL is permanently broken and the import is never retried. Check post.persisted? / post.errors.empty? instead of post.present?.

findings.title: absolutize_urls mangles protocol-relative URLs
findings.body: Both the and rewriting treat any value starting with '/' as root-relative and rewrite it to prefix + path. Protocol-relative URLs such as //cdn.example.com/image.png (common in feeds and CMS output) also start with '/', so they are rewritten to http://host/cdn.example.com/image.png, breaking the link or image. Values starting with '//' should be left alone.

findings.title: Unauthenticated endpoint enqueues unbounded outbound-fetch jobs
findings.body: Any GET to /embed/best whose Referer host matches embeddable_host (a header trivially forged by non-browser clients) and that carries a previously unseen embed_url enqueues a RetrieveTopic job, which performs an outbound HTTP fetch of that URL. The only throttle is a 60-second redis key per URL inside the job, so an attacker can enqueue unlimited jobs simply by varying the URL — exhausting sidekiq workers and directing a flood of fetches at the configured embeddable host. There should be a global or per-IP rate limit before enqueuing retrieval work.

findings.title: Every new embed URL runs a full synchronous feed poll
findings.body: When feed_polling_enabled? is on, perform_retrieve executes Jobs::PollFeed inline for each retrieval before falling back to direct HTTP fetch. The retrieval throttle is keyed per embed URL, so N distinct new embed URLs cause N full feed downloads/parses (and a re-import/revision pass over every feed item) inside RetrieveTopic jobs. The unused feed_key method on PollFeed suggests a per-feed throttle was intended but never wired up.

findings.title: Missing Referer hard-fails embedding for legitimate visitors
findings.body: ensure_embeddable raises Discourse::InvalidAccess when request.referer is blank. Visitors using referer-stripping privacy extensions, behind referer-removing proxies, or on an HTTPS page embedding an HTTP forum (browsers omit Referer on the HTTPS→HTTP downgrade) will get an error instead of the comment embed. The check only needs to reject referers from foreign hosts; a blank referer could be treated as allowed so these users still see comments.

findings.title: Disqus import no longer preserves the thread's original creation date
findings.body: Before this change the topic-opening post was created with created_at: Date.parse(t[:created_at]); the new code path calls TopicEmbed.import_remote(user, t[:link], title: t[:title]), which provides no way to pass created_at, so every imported thread's opening post is timestamped at import time. Imported forums lose their original chronology (topic ordering, 'x days ago' dates, digest ordering). Add a created_at option to import/import_remote and pass the thread date through.
